description: Fix error and warning findings, and restore anything listed in designRemovals. Info findings are not problems (the email falls back safely there): never remove responsive (@media), dark-mode CSS or rounded corners to clear them. designRemovals compares this version with the first one audited for the same email (or with previousHtml): design the edits deleted, such as @media rules, dark mode, corners, gradients, VML fallbacks or images. Comprehensive email quality audit: CSS compatibility, spam scoring, link validation, accessibility, images, inbox preview, size (Gmail clipping), template variables, content overflow, visual fallbacks, dark-mode and mobile text contrast, design consistency, structural faults in Outlook-only VML (which lives inside conditional comments and is invisible to every other check), style survival: CSS a client parses correctly and then discards, such as a stylesheet past Gmail's 16 KB ceiling or every rule after a `}}`, which no support matrix can express, and client targeting: HowToTarget hacks such as Gmail u+.body or MSO conditionals, which do not score as css-hack. For HTML input, findings tied to a specific element carry loc (line, column, offset) so you can edit the exact source. Compatibility is collapsed to one finding per problem listing the clients it affects; pass detail:'full' for the per-client breakdown with fix snippets. Use skip to omit checks, targetingPolicy to change how targeted scopes affect scores, and clients to narrow which clients are reported.

clients.description: Only report these client IDs (e.g. ['gmail-web','outlook-windows']). The fastest way to cut the response when you care about specific clients. Use list_clients for the IDs.

detail.description: 'summary' (default) returns one entry per error or warning, listing the clients it affects, and only counts info findings (safe fallbacks). 'full' returns one entry per client with fix snippets, info included.

emailType.description: 'transactional' (receipts, password resets, codes, alerts: no unsubscribe link required) or 'marketing'. Omitted: guessed from the content, which misses many transactional emails.

format.description: Source format: 'html' (default), 'jsx' (React Email), 'mjml', or 'maizzle' (HTML template or Vue single-file component). Anything but 'html' is compiled before analysis and sets the syntax of the fix snippets. A pasted Vue file with no format is compiled as maizzle.

html.description: The email source: HTML, or an MJML / Maizzle / React Email template when `format` says so. Pass this or `path`.

path.description: Absolute path to the email source file (.html, .htm, .mjml, .jsx, .tsx, .vue), instead of `html`. Prefer it when the email is on disk: the source stays out of your context. The extension sets `format` unless you pass one.

previousHtml.description: The design to hold this version to, usually your first draft. Omitted: the first version of this email audited in this session (matched by <title> and text).

targetingPolicy.description: 'progressive' (default) suppresses compatibility false-positives inside client-targeted scopes and only flags deprecated or dangerous hacks. 'strict' treats targeting as non-standard and reports every hack. 'lenient' suppresses false positives and ignores non-fatal targeting warnings.
